newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Surgeon says Yeltsin ignored advice on heart.
newsitem.headline: Surgeon says Yeltsin ignored advice on heart.

text.p: President Boris Yeltsin's heart surgeon said on Sunday the Russian leader had worsened his heart condition by ignoring medical advice and subjecting himself to "inhuman" levels of stress.

Renat Akchurin, speaking to Russian television, confirmed that Yeltsin's heart was in such poor shape in August after several months of an exhausting re-election campaign that doctors had serious doubts whether an operation was possible.

"We are talking about a patient who, for the last eight months, experienced enormous, inhuman stresses...Physical stresses were accompanied by emotional ones as well as serious attacks of stenocardia. But, treating himself ruthlessly, he managed to go and meet the people next day."
He said that as far as he knew between the two rounds of the election Yeltsin had a most serious bout of stenocardia -- heart pain or angina -- but added he could not exclude a minor heart attack.

"Nevertheless Boris Nikolayevich, paying no attention whatsoever to recommendations by the doctors -- and I know it from his medical records -- first spoke to intellectuals and then moved to another city and continued his election campaign".

A panel of experts decided on Wednesday that Yeltsin's bypass operation should go ahead, but not for six or eight weeks. Yeltsin, who has delegated part of his authority to Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin, will have to stay in hospital until then and face a lengthy convalescence afterwards.

"In August we received a coronary patient in grave condition. Naturally, serious doubts arose whether to operate," Akchurin said. "But the following month and a half has shown that the myocardiac function is improving and the risk is smaller."
Akchurin said that the aim of the delay in carrying out the operation was to make Yeltsin a routine patient rather than an emergency one.
